evidence: TaskManagementService constructor injects UserRepository, ProjectRepository and TaskRepository interfaces from the domain, so it orchestrates through ports instead of doing persistence itself
completeTask() calls markDone() from the domain for the state change, then saves through this.tasks.save()
requireText() and the dueDate checks in addTask() validate and normalize untyped input (unknown) at the use-case boundary
requireProject/requireTask/requireUser check that entities exist and throw domain NotFoundError/ValidationError; no HTTP status codes or transport concerns
randomUUID() from node:crypto is used only to generate IDs, which is acceptable in an application service
parsedVerdict.reasoning: src/application/services.ts does the work of an application-layer use-case service. TaskManagementService coordinates domain repositories that it receives as interfaces, checks and normalizes untyped input at the use-case boundary, generates IDs and decides what to save. The one real domain state change, completing a task, is handed to the domain through markDone(). The file has no persistence code: it only calls repository interfaces and uses no SQL or storage APIs. It has no transport or framework code either: no HTTP request or response objects, status codes or routing. Building Task objects inline with defaults (status 'todo', description '') and checking title, description and dueDate could arguably sit in a domain factory, which points to a thin domain model. Still, this is normal input validation for a use case and not a misplaced responsibility. No ADR text was given that contradicts this.
